input.summary: Full ledger built and traced against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (the YOU passage describing a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is drafting-agent prose, carries no authority, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities). Every limitation of all 17 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-13 installed assembly, 14-17 method) was traced to affirmative disclosure text: semicircular halves, hinge end/latch end, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads and the no-tool-specific-diameter result, outward carriage springs, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by frame closure, followers in oblique slots, wedge on a ring drive face, limited stroke, synchronized inward travel, force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge, indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, the non-participating mounting boss, and the install/remove sequences. All 28 numerals in draft/numerals.md were checked for a single consistent referent, for appearance in the detailed description, and for presence in at least one figure brief; no numeral is orphaned, duplicated, or reused for a second part, and the unused value 28 creates no conflict. All six figure briefs were compared line by line against draft/07-drawings.md and the detailed description; the FIG. 3 / FIG. 6 cross-references, the FIGS. 3 and 4 cross-reference for numeral 54, and the FIGS. 2 and 5 cross-reference for numerals 22/24 are consistent. No sectional views or section designations exist, so that check is moot. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any draft file, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language was added to justify a renderer's shape choice. Background prior-art characterizations were treated as not requiring inventor support. Three findings are reported. The one critical item is a functional-surface geometry assertion: both FIG-3 and FIG-6 place the cam ring drive face "adjacent to the right junction," which fixes the circumferential end position of a functional drive face relative to the segment junction; the disclosure says only that "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring," never where on the ring that face lies or that drive enters the ring at a segment end. Two minor items: the mounting boss is briefed as projecting "radially outward from the outer boundary" in FIG-1 and FIG-2 where the source says only "outside the annular guide," and the figure briefs designate numerals 24 and 36 as "slideway" and "channel" while the specification and numeral table call them "radial guide" and "annular guide." Note also, per the drafting brief, that no prior-art search was run and the art supplied in prior_art/ may be incomplete; that does not affect the source-fidelity conclusions above.

findings.title: Cam ring drive face given an untraced circumferential end position adjacent to the segment junction
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (Geometry to draw, bullet 4; Numeral placement target 54) and figures/FIG-6.md (Geometry to draw, final bullet)
findings.detail: Both briefs fix the circumferential position of the ring drive face (numeral 54) relative to the right-hand segment junction. For a functional drive face, a circumferential end position is substantive technical matter even where the brief says the geometry is schematic: placing the face immediately beside the junction asserts that latch drive enters the ring at the very end of one segment and reaches the other segment only through the coupling faces. The disclosure never states where on the cam ring the drive face lies. It states only that the wedge is driven against a drive face of the cam ring, and separately that the complementary faces couple the segments. No affirmative USER passage locates the drive face at, near, or adjacent to a junction, or at a segment end.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-3): "A short drive face is located on the ring adjacent to the right junction." and numeral target "54: the short drive face beside the right junction." Candidate (FIG-6): "A drive face from FIG. 3 is shown schematically on the band adjacent to the right junction, without a numeral." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md, paragraph 2), which shows the gap: "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." The disclosure contains no statement of where that drive face is located on the ring.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md replace the bullet with: "A short drive face is located on the ring band, at a place clear of the slots and clear of both junctions." and replace the numeral target with: "54: the short drive face on the ring band, clear of both junctions." In figures/FIG-6.md replace the final geometry bullet with: "A drive face from FIG. 3 is shown schematically on the band, clear of both junctions, without a numeral." No change is required to draft/08-detailed-description.md or draft/09-claims.md, which recite only "a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30" without a position.

findings.title: Mounting boss briefed as projecting radially outward beyond the frame outer boundary
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md (Geometry to draw, mounting boss bullet) and figures/FIG-2.md (Geometry to draw, mounting boss bullet)
findings.detail: The briefs assert a specific relative location for the mounting boss (numeral 66): that it projects radially outward from the outer boundary of the frame, i.e. that it extends beyond the frame periphery. The disclosure locates the boss only as being "outside the annular guide," which does not say whether it stands radially beyond the frame periphery or on an axial face of the frame outside the annular guide. The specification text itself is correctly neutral ("The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36."), so only the figure briefs overreach. The requirement that the boss be drawn clear of the hinge and latch is non-substantive page placement for legibility and may remain.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-1): "A mounting boss projects radially outward from the outer boundary of the frame, at a place clear of the hinge and of the latch so that it is separately visible." Candidate (FIG-2): "A mounting boss projects radially outward from the outer boundary of the annular body." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md, final paragraph): "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit." There is no source statement that the boss projects radially outward or lies beyond the frame's outer boundary.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md replace with: "A mounting boss is shown schematically on the frame, at a place clear of the hinge and of the latch so that it is separately visible." In figures/FIG-2.md replace with: "A mounting boss is shown schematically on the annular body outside the channel that holds the cam ring." Leave the numeral 66 placement targets unchanged.

findings.title: Figure briefs designate numerals 24 and 36 with terms that differ from the specification and numeral table
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md and figures/FIG-5.md (geometry bullets and numeral placement targets for 24 and 36); compare draft/numerals.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md
findings.detail: The same numbered parts are designated by different terms across the record. Numeral 24 is "radial guide" in the numeral table, the description and the claims, but is called a "slideway" throughout FIG-2 and FIG-5. Numeral 36 is "annular guide" in the numeral table, the description and the claims, but is called a "channel" in FIG-2. The referents are unambiguous, so this is not a numeral collision, but the designations should be repeated identically so each numbered part is named one way in every view and in the drawing description.
findings.evidence: draft/numerals.md: "| 24 | radial guide |" and "| 36 | annular guide |". draft/08-detailed-description.md: "each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame" and "A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame." figures/FIG-2.md: "Three radial slideways are spaced around the annular body"; "A narrow cam ring is located within a channel in the annular body"; "24: well inside the lower left slideway"; "36: the channel that holds the cam ring". figures/FIG-5.md: "two parallel radial lines defining a slideway"; "24: the left one of the two parallel lines defining the slideway."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md substitute "radial guide" for "slideway"/"slideways" and "annular guide" for "channel" throughout, giving: "A narrow cam ring is located within an annular guide in the annular body"; "Three radial guides are spaced around the annular body"; "A carriage is located in each of the three radial guides"; "24: well inside the lower left radial guide, clear of the carriage in it"; "36: the annular guide that holds the cam ring, at a place clear of the carriages". In figures/FIG-5.md substitute "radial guide" for "slideway" throughout, giving: "two parallel radial lines defining a radial guide", "...guided by the radial guide", "...the zigzag lying parallel to the radial guide...toward the upper end of the radial guide", and "24: the left one of the two parallel lines defining the radial guide."
